ordinary_request_ack.ptd_die: requested die when multi-PMP bit 0 is set; otherwise die 0
ordinary_request_ack.request: read-modify-write; clear for state 0, set for state 1
ordinary_request_ack.success: newData is set and the selected ack bit equals the request
ordinary_request_ack.poll_deadline_observed_use: recomputed in the loop but never read by this function
ordinary_request_ack.request_after_success: preserved; there is no second PTD write
ordinary_request_ack.pre_ready_behavior: publish the persistent request, sample PMP-STATUS, and return success without reading PS-ACK when status is zero
ordinary_request_ack.ready_behavior: latch the per-die ready byte and poll PS-ACK when PMP-STATUS is nonzero
ordinary_request_ack.timeout: dump the PMPTOOL PTD range and panic

state_notification.target: public handle at +0x1a, selector byte at +3 if zero
state_notification.initial_precondition: wait for dependent cluster transition bytes to become stable
state_notification.initial_precondition_scope: cluster power only; it does not read ApplePTD or call the PMP-ready wait

readiness.dynamic_transition_order: checkNotifyPMP, wait until ready, mutate device state, then emit command 14/15
readiness.initial_sync: scheduled separately; it may publish level requests before ready, and the ordinary transaction then bypasses PS-ACK while status is zero

initial_publication.command_selection: command 14, or 15 when the signed DeviceData flag byte is negative
initial_publication.order: ApplePMGR::start runs the whole publication inside _initPMPv2, so every initial level request precedes the first readiness observation; it is deliberate, not a race

interrupt_config.scope: the runtime property is the boot DeviceTree pmgr property merged with its selected variant overlay, so the per-die count must be read at run time rather than assumed

ready_close.effect: latch the per-die ready byte, then command-gate wake every waiter
ready_close.secondary_source: _waitForPMPReadyActionGatedv2 latches the same byte on its own when the PTD PMP-STATUS entry becomes nonzero, so the interrupt is not the only way the handshake closes

read.operation: one 16-byte load of data and raw metadata

decoded_entry.caller_tag: decoded metadata bits 56..63, retained from output +0xf

ptd_transport.range_check: entry_count must be nonzero; callers supply the entry index
ptd_transport.ordering: no explicit lock or DMB/DSB appears in the UUID-pinned read, write, or final register-store sequence; ordering depends on the Device MMIO mapping

rtbuddy_fixup.scope: image preparation and RTBuddy bookkeeping only; no PMP run-state or dashboard-ready acknowledgement is established

writable.device_tree_rule: writable when DeviceTree flag bit 0 is clear

dart_skip.meaning: iBoot already installed this mapping; do not insert it

segment_flags.scope: bit 0 is read-only and bit 1 is iBoot-installed; they are distinct and a record commonly sets one without the other

host_copy.scope: the whole padded region is copied into host memory once and cached; edits never touch the target directly

edit.scope: the record value is edited in place in the host copy and the bay is marked dirty; a record whose length is not four is fatal here rather than skipped

write_back.bounds: the padded region must lie wholly inside the read-write map
write_back.scope: the entire region is pushed back with 32-bit stores, which is why the located region is aligned down and padded up to four

identity_block.base: the coredump map's IOP virtual base, or zero when absent

region.iop_virtual: identity base + the block's patchbay offset
region.align_pad: the low two bits of the unaligned address
region.writable: the containing segment is writable, or no segment claims the address at all

record.tag_byte_order: the driver's u32 constant spells the tag most-significant byte first, so the bytes stored in the image are reversed

firmware_source.skip_firmware_service_rule: set when the nub publishes `running` or `no-firmware-service`; `pre-loaded` alone never sets it

selection.path: wait for an RTBuddyFirmwareService matching the role

iboot_loaded.scope: an image adopted from the DeviceTree segment map; a firmware service always produces a non-iBoot image that is copied to the target unless one is already mapped

firmware_source.scope: this is the image-provenance decision only; it is independent of whether AppleA7IOP treats the nub's DART records as iBoot-owned

managed_cpu_start.completion: enter IOP validation immediately after CPU start

rtkit_handshake.validation_target_selection: status 6 when RTBuddy byte 0x100 or 0x108 is set; otherwise status 8

reply.payload: a bitmap of the endpoints the host already has in that group, so the first reply sets only bit 0 and only for group 0

endpoint_roll_call.scope: Endpoint1 is a service-name suffix, not RTKit wire endpoint 1

rtkit_handshake.scope: RTBuddy transport and endpoint discovery only; it does not prove ApplePMGR observed PMP-STATUS or an AGX dashboard ack
